_comment: WhiteKnights (2026-09-27). PINS THE ONE DEPTH AT WHICH ACCLAIMED CONTENDER'S DIG CONVERTS. Contender's ETB digs 5 and may put a Knight in hand; MTG_ACQ_DIG (default ON) is what lets the second pass spend the turn's leftover mana on the card just acquired. That lever is DEPTH-0-ONLY by construction (AIEngine.cpp: 'MTG_ACQ_DIG is deliberately ABSENT here: the lever is depth-0-only'; EngineFlags: 'searched byte-identical by construction'), and site 10's general 'the hand gained a card' rule does NOT cover this card either -- ParamKeyedDrawClass claims any etb_dig_count > 0 cast, in BOTH worlds, so the general rule explicitly carves Contender out. This fixture is therefore a guard on the d0 mechanism, the only path that works, and depth 0 is load-bearing rather than incidental: measured at this exact board, d0 deploys the dug Knight on turn 4 and d1/d3/d5 all decline it (deterministic, budget-independent up to d9/5000ms). Board: 4 untapped Plains and one Venerable Knight, which is required -- etb_dig_requires_subtypes means the dig does not happen at all without ANOTHER Knight. Hand: Contender alone. Library stacked so index 0 is a Plains that absorbs the draw step and the Knight sits at index 1, inside the top-5 window rather than being drawn. Correct line: cast Contender for {2}{W}, dig, take the Knight, cast it with the fourth Plains the same main phase. ASSERT ON OPPONENT LIFE, not the win turn: both behaviours win on turn 7, so the win turn does not discriminate -- the same-turn deploy is worth exactly the 2 extra damage the 2/1 gets from its one extra attack, which is -3 here versus -1 when the deploy is declined. The searched-depth gap is an OPEN DEFECT recorded in docs/design/contender-same-turn-deploy-searched.md, not something this fixture blesses.
